core_job: The shopping trip, for a household grocery shopper who buys around an allergy or a diet. Build the list by typing, pasting or camera-scanning. The list is grouped by aisle and saved on the phone. Pick a nearby supermarket that is open (OSM Overpass, with opening_hours parsed). Then shop in a large-type trip mode, tick items off, and keep finished trips in a searchable history you can re-add from. You send the list through the share sheet and import it by pasting. It does not sync live between phones. No account, no prices.
signature: Basket check: allergy-aware swaps to better Nutri-Scores, inside the list you shop from. You set a household allergen profile on the phone, using Open Food Facts allergen tags. Each list item can be linked to a real OFF product, and then shows its Nutri-Score plus a 'Contains milk' chip if it clashes with the profile. Basket check shows the A–E grade mix, then finds alternatives for items graded D/E or that clash with the profile. Alternatives come from the same most-specific en: category through search-a-licious: a better grade, sold in your country, none of the profile allergens. Before any alternative is shown, its own OFF product record is fetched again. This step is required because I found the search index wrong today: 2 of 12 gluten-free cereal hits actually contain gluten, and one is graded c, not b. Swap replaces the item in place, with Undo and a saved swap log. Competitors were checked through the keyless iTunes API, because web search is disabled here. Yuka's App Store listing mentions alternatives but no shopping list. The OurGroceries, AnyList and Bring! listings mention shared lists and aisles but no nutrition grades or allergens. These claims cover their store listings only; I did not install the apps.
